cards.explanation: The answer is True. Persia's fourth king will be far richer than all the others. That's not a man with a nice savings account, friends. That's a man whose couch cushions have couch cushions.
The answer is Greece. By the power of his wealth, Persia's fourth king will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece. Everyone, friends. That's a group chat you do NOT want to be added to.
The answer is False. Daniel 11:4 says the mighty king's kingdom will not go to his descendants. It's uprooted and given to others instead. A kingdom that big, and nobody in the family gets the keys.

The answer is that the commander will rule his own kingdom with great authority. The king of the South grows strong, but one of his commanders grows even stronger. That's the employee who gets promoted right past the boss, friends. Awkward at the next meeting, I bet.

The answer is to seal the agreement. After some years the South and the North form an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the South goes to the king of the North to seal it. That's the reason the text gives, friends.

The answer is that he will enter the fortress and prevail. One from the daughter's family line comes against the army of the king of the North, enters his fortress, fighting and prevailing. He doesn't just knock on the gate, friends. He walks right in.

The answer is gods. The text says, “He will take even their gods captive to Egypt…” and the metal images and precious vessels of silver and gold come along with them. It's a whole moving truck of the North's treasures. That's quite a haul, friends.

The answer is a great army. The sons of the king of the North stir up strife and assemble a great army, which advances forcefully, sweeping through like a flood. A flood doesn't ask permission, friends. Strife comes first, and then the army.

The answer is that he marches out in a rage to fight. When the North's army carries the battle as far as the fortress, the king of the South marches out in a rage against the king of the North. He doesn't wait for the doorbell, friends. He's already out the door.

The answer is False. When the army is carried off, the king of the South will be proud in heart and cast down tens of thousands, but he will not triumph. Proud heart, tens of thousands cast down, and still no triumph. Winning the fight without winning the whole thing is a strange spot to be in, friends.

The answer is that it will be larger than the first. The king of the North will raise another army, larger than the first, with many supplies. He lost one army and came back with a bigger one, friends. Daniel 11:13 says he does it after some years.
The answer is fail. The violent ones among Daniel's own people will exalt themselves in fulfillment of the vision, but they will fail. A big rise doesn't promise a big finish, friends.

The answer is that even their best troops won't be able to resist. When the king of the North captures a fortified city, the forces of the South will not stand. When the best can't hold, you know it's a hard day. Verse 15 says it plainly, friends.

The answer is a daughter in marriage. The king of the North gives the king of the South a daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom. The agreement and the plan are two different things, friends. Daniel 11:17 puts them side by side.
The answer is False. Daniel 11:17 says his plan will not succeed or help him. All that scheming, and the plan goes nowhere. Not succeeding is the whole story of that plan, friends.

The answer is True. After the king of the North turns his face to the coastlands and captures many of them, a commander puts an end to his reproach and turns it back upon him. He gets a taste of his own medicine, friends. The reproach he dished out comes right back around.

The answer is that he will stumble and fall and be no more. The king of the North turns back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and be no more. I think this one is heavy, friends, so let it sit for a second.
The answer is False. Daniel 11:20 says within a few days he will be destroyed, though not in anger or in battle. So the battle part is what doesn't fit. The text says how it won't happen, friends.

The answer is that he will seize it by intrigue in a time of peace. Royal honors will not be given to the despicable person, but he comes in a time of peace and seizes the kingdom by intrigue. Intrigue is how he seizes it, friends. It's peace on the outside and scheming doing the work.

The answer is False. Daniel 11:23 says that after an alliance is made with the despicable person, he will act deceitfully. He rises to power with only a few people, yet he acts deceitfully. Watch who you shake hands with, friends.

The answer is that he will lavish it on his followers. The despicable person lavishes plunder, loot, and wealth on his followers. I bet his followers have no complaints, friends. Verse 24 names them as the ones who get it.

The answer is the plots devised against him. The king of the South mobilizes a very large and powerful army, but he will not withstand the plots devised against him. A big army, and still the plots get him, friends. Plans made against him are what he can't stand up to.

The answer is True. Those who eat from the king of the South's provisions will seek to destroy him. It's like biting the hand that fills the cookie jar, friends. The people eating his provisions are the ones seeking to destroy him.

The answer is that the end will still come at the appointed time. The two kings speak lies at the same table, but to no avail, for still the end will come at the appointed time. That's the reason the verse gives, friends. Their lies don't change it.

The answer is that he will lose heart and turn back. The ships of Kittim come against the king of the North, and he loses heart and turns back. All that power, and his heart drops when the ships show up, friends. The ships of Kittim are what do it.

The answer is False. Daniel 11:30 says the king of the North will return and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant. The favor goes to the people walking away from it, friends. Rage first, then favor for those who forsake it.
The answer is resist. The text says, “…the people who know their God will firmly resist him.” He corrupts with flattery, and they hold firm. That's a steady kind of strong, friends.

The answer is so they may be refined and purified. That's the reason the text gives for why some of the wise will fall. The verse says, “…so that they may be refined, purified, and made spotless…” I think this part is heavy, friends, so I'll let the verse speak for itself.
